key_insight: A single 3D segmentation model can learn pancreas anatomy across both CT and MRI by aligning features from different modalities, reducing the need for separate labeled datasets. This enables better cross-modality transfer, especially for pancreas subregion segmentation.
problem_solved: Medical image segmentation models often fail when moved from one imaging modality to another because CT and MRI look very different. This paper addresses the challenge of building a label-efficient model that generalizes across modalities and supports subregion transfer.
method: Train a unified 3D pancreas segmentation framework on 4,604 heterogeneous CT and MRI scans.
Use domain-adversarial learning to reduce modality-specific differences and learn shared anatomical representations.
Adopt a shared nnU-Net encoder-decoder architecture to perform whole-pancreas segmentation and support cross-modality subregion transfer.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows a practical path toward more robust medical segmentation systems that work across scanners and imaging types. It can reduce annotation burden and improve real-world deployment where modality shift is common.

paper_title: Unified CT and MRI Pancreas Segmentation for Label-Efficient Cross-Modality Subregion Transfer
